sections.title: Conditional expectation: existence, versions and defining identities

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-conditional-expectation-C002 (partial): The construction or argument is not written in full. In annex:p15.conditional-existence (handbook/annex/p15/conditional-expectation.tex lines 23-31) P is restricted to G and the proved Radon-Nikodym theorem is applied on (Omega,G,P|_G). That gives nu_pm(A) = int_A Z_pm d(P|_G). Lines 32-39 then say Z_pm are integrable with integrals EX^pm and write int_A Z dP = nu_+(A) - nu_-(A). This quietly swaps P|_G-integrals of G-measurable functions for P-integrals. No step or citation supports that swap, and no handbook result states it. It would follow from thm:p15-expectation-law-integral applied to the identity map (Omega,F0)->(Omega,G), or from G-simple approximation (thm:p15-measurable-limits) plus monotone convergence on both spaces. As written, the argument that the constructed Z satisfies the P-integral identity and P-integrability required by def:p15-general-conditional-expectation has an unwritten step. Every other element is present: integrability and E|Z|<=E|X| (annex 5-14), a.e. uniqueness (15-21), the source's X+/X- construction (23-39; Durrett p. 207, PDF 215), no completion (41), and the worked a.e.-uniqueness boundary (body 365-371, annex 727-739).
